message.content:
The sculpture most often cited as the quintessential icon of 19th‑century art is **Auguste Rodin’s “The Thinker”** (originally conceived as part of his monumental work *The Gates of Hell*, 1880–1902).  

Rodin’s bronze figure—an introspective, muscular man hunched over in deep contemplation—has become a cultural shorthand for intellectualism and artistic genius. Its dramatic realism, expressive form, and the way it captures a universal human moment have made it one of the most reproduced and celebrated sculptures of the era, appearing in countless museums, public spaces, and popular media worldwide.
